extracted.intended_audience: students and early-career mathematicians (primary school through postdoc) and those seeking academic career guidance in mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Short, stage-by-stage career advice for people pursuing mathematics (from gifted primary-school students to undergraduates, graduate students, and postdocs), emphasizing research practice, professional development, and practical decisions. The page collects concise maxims and pointers about study choices, research habits, presentations, and career decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't base career decisions on glamour or fame
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't base career decisions on glamour or fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied guidance: evaluate career choices on substance and fit rather than perceived prestige; follow up link/context suggests studying at different places as an alternative consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study at different places
rubrics_metrics.description: But you should study at different places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to experience multiple institutions/environments during training to broaden exposure and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on mathematics competitions (high school)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted guidance for high-school level students about participating in competitions (link provided); implies competitions are a useful formative activity at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work hard and work professionally; enjoy your work
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to work hard, and work professionally. But it is also important to enjoy your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance: sustain professional standards and effort while preserving intrinsic enjoyment of mathematics; both are important for long-term success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think ahead and ask dumb questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Think ahead to understand the way forward; ask yourself dumb questions to understand the way before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan research direction proactively and use simple/basic questions to clarify understanding of the research path; anticipating the next steps helps progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend talks and conferences broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend talks and conferences, even those not directly related to your own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden exposure to new ideas and communities; serendipitous connections and cross-disciplinary ideas can benefit research and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk to your advisor but take initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to your advisor, but also take the initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advisor guidance while driving your own research agenda; don't be overly passive—proactively propose directions, projects, and solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't prematurely obsess on a single 'big problem' or 'big theory'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't prematurely obsess on a single 'big problem' or 'big theory'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid early fixation that can limit exploration and growth; explore multiple directions before committing to a long-term focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write down what you've done and make your work available
rubrics_metrics.description: Write down what you've done, and make your work available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation and dissemination are critical—maintain written records and share preprints/papers; the author links to further advice on how to write and submit papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn and relearn your field; learn outside your field
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn and relearn your field, but don't be afraid to learn things outside your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continual updating of knowledge in one's specialty while acquiring tools and perspectives from other areas to expand problem-solving capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn the limitations of your tools and the power of others' tools; aim just beyond your range
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the limitations of your tools, but also learn the power of other mathematician's tools. In particular, you should continually aim just beyond your current range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be realistic about what your current methods can achieve; actively acquire new techniques from others and choose problems that stretch but do not vastly exceed your capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible and patient in research
rubrics_metrics.description: In your research, be both flexible and patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to change approaches or directions as needed and recognize that meaningful progress can take time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and present your research; be considerate of your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: You should definitely travel and present your research if given the opportunity. But be considerate of your audience; talks are not the same as papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take opportunities to give talks and network; adapt exposition to the format and audience—oral presentations require different emphasis and style than written papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sceptical of your own work and willing to discard it
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sceptical of your own work, and don't be afraid to use the wastebasket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt critical self-evaluation; remove or abandon ideas/results that don't hold up rather than clinging to them for pride or sunk-cost reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documented external resources and mentorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek and consult other career-advice resources and mentors (links to John Baez, Fan Chung, Alain Connes, AMS advice page for new PhDs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a variety of perspectives—read established guides and discuss decisions with advisors or mentors who know your specific situation; the page explicitly recommends discussing important decisions with your advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider gifted-education options at primary level
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For younger students, consider specialized education pathways appropriate for gifted learners (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on problem-solving beyond grades and formal rigor (undergraduate)
rubrics_metrics.description: How can one become better at solving mathematical problems? Note that there is more to maths than grades and exams and methods; there is also more to maths than rigour and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize problem-solving skills, intuition, and creativity beyond merely obtaining high grades or perfect formalism; cultivate a broader mathematical understanding.
